jobs.jobDescription:
KPMG China provides multidisciplinary services from audit and tax to advisory, with a strong focus on serving our clients’ needs and their industries. Not only do we have an overriding commitment to provide the highest quality services for our clients, but we also strive to become a responsible corporate citizen that has a positive impact on our environment and community. At KPMG, you’ll translate insights into action and reveal opportunities for all—our teams, our clients and our world.

 

Service Line Overview

The Office of the General Counsel (“OGC”) of KPMG China is a diverse and dynamic organization within our firm, headed up by the General Counsel, with approximately 32 lawyers plus approximately 6 practice protection senior

managers and managers within KPMG China. The OGC provides comprehensive legal services and broad risk management support to our firm’s leadership, functions and support staff.


We are seeking a mid-level experienced Company Secretary / Corporate Secretarial Manager to manage corporate secretarial, entity governance and statutory compliance matters for KPMG China’s group entities in Mainland China, Hong Kong and other offshore jurisdictions. This individual will report to the Office of General Counsel.


Key Responsibilities

  • Manage day-to-day corporate secretarial administration and entity governance for KPMG group entities, working closely with Legal, Finance, Tax, HR and business stakeholders or coordinating with external registered agents and corporate service providers.
  • Own the central internal entity database and corporate calendar, applying consistent processes and documentation standards across the group while meeting local requirements.
  • Coordinate statutory and regulatory filings and annual compliance requirements with local authorities and service providers.
  • Prepare corporate approvals, resolutions, minutes, powers of attorney and other governance documents for group entities; support Board and shareholder matters and coordinate execution, notarisation and legalisation where required.
  • Handle changes to directors, officers, registered information and other corporate particulars for group entities.
  • Support incorporations, restructurings, de-registrations and other corporate transactions.


Experience & Background

  • University degree in Accounting, Finance, Legal or a related discipline.
  • 3 to 5 years of experience handling group company corporate secretarial matters. Qualification as a company secretary in Hong Kong or other jurisdictions will be more highly preferred.
  • Work experience with top law firms or listed multi-national corporations in their company secretarial department will be looked upon more favourably.
  • Strong organisational skills and ability to manage multiple entities, jurisdictions and deadlines.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word, with strong overall Microsoft Office skills.
  • Fluent written and spoken Chinese (Cantonese and Mandarin) and English, including the ability to work with corporate documentation in both languages.


About KPMG

At KPMG China, we are committed to being an equal opportunity employer, with zero tolerance for any form of discrimination against any persons. It is important for us to create an inclusive, diverse and agile workplace for our people to develop and thrive at both a personal and professional level.

 

We strive to make ESG (environmental, social and governance) a watermark running through our organisation; from empowering our people to become agents of positive change, to providing better solutions and services to our clients to help them achieve their ESG goals. View Our Impact Plan to learn more about our ESG commitments and progress across four key pillars - Governance, People, Planet and Prosperity – and how we make a positive impact on our people, environment and society.

We encourage you to come as you are, and we welcome all qualified candidates to apply, and hope you unlock opportunities with us. Visit KPMG China website for more company information. 

 

You acknowledge and agree that all personal information hereby provided regarding yourself will be used by KPMG China for its candidate selection purposed only. KPMG China collects, uses, processes, and retains your personal information in accordance with KPMG China’s Online Privacy Statement and/or KPMG China Privacy Statement (collectively "Privacy Statement"). During the recruitment process, KPMG China may need to store personal information of candidates in a designated third-party application tracking platform.

 

If you have any questions regarding the information you provided in the form or your job application in general, please contact KPMG China’s HR personnel in the location where your application is submitted [see here].

Service Line Overview

KPMG's People Services team provides compensation and employment related advice and insights to clients that help organisations attract, engage and retain their key executives and broader workforce, with a particular focus on internationally mobile employees.

 

Our service covers the development of policies and related remuneration packages, cross-border solutions between Hong Kong and other jurisdictions, reviews of international assignment programmes, pensions, tax, human resources advice, completion of tax returns (for PRC and Hong Kong) for assignees and advanced technology-based solutions. The People Services portfolio ranges from large multinational companies to local start-ups.

 

We are now seeking high-calibre tax professionals support the continued growth of our People Services team in Hong Kong. The ideal candidate will bring a commercial and analytical mind and have solid advisory skills. Knowledge of the Hong Kong tax system is essential. Knowledge of Mainland China is a plus.


Key Responsibilities

  • Have a very strong understanding of Hong Kong tax legislation and be able to apply it to various client matters
  • Work with clients to develop tax efficient solutions to address their business needs
  • Participate in business development activities and gain new work from existing clients
  • Coach junior members of staff to help them achieve their goals. They will also review and manage their staff's work
  • Use knowledge of relevant non-tax legal, financial and business information
  • Regularly expand their knowledge of the tax business and keep up-to-date with the latest business and current affairs as it relates to their clients
  • Deal with tax authority enquiries in an effective manner


Experience & Background

  • A degree in Accounting / Finance / Law / Engineering preferred or any other business-related discipline is required, as well as a professional qualification
  • Minimum of 6 years' tax experience in a professional firm.
  • Experience in handling complex technical issues concerning employee remuneration e.g., equity plans, dual contracts, pensions, etc
  • Excellent written and spoken Chinese (Mandarin and Cantonese) and English.

  • Well-organized with ability to meet multiple deadlines and work under pressure
